title: Too many redirects, then an untrusted certificate

source.title: ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS after adding SSL using LE (Let's Encrypt Community)

brief:
**PAGE 11:05 · shop.example.com · new web VM**

The new web VM was provisioned with a script this morning. Three reports so far:

- Browsers say **ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS** on every shop page.
- A colleague ran `curl http://127.0.0.1/` on the box, got "Welcome to nginx!" and concluded the shop isn't deployed.
- The health check `curl -fsS https://shop.example.com/health` fails with `curl: (60) SSL certificate problem`. Someone suggested adding `-k`.

The certificate comes from our internal CA (`/etc/ssl/example-ca/`). `shop.example.com` resolves to this box. Use curl to see what really happens, then fix the server and the trust, not the client flags.

tasks.title: Follow the redirects
tasks.text:
First explain the "Welcome to nginx" report: one IP serves several sites, and nginx picks the server block from one request header. Compare `curl -sI http://127.0.0.1/` with `curl -sI http://shop.example.com/`.

Then follow the chain: `curl -skIL --max-redirs 5 https://shop.example.com/docs/`. Find the config line that redirects HTTPS to itself and fix it so HTTPS serves files (and 404 for missing ones). Keep the single HTTP→HTTPS redirect. Done when HTTPS pages answer 200 with no redirect.
hints: `curl -v` shows the `Host:` header curl sends. Every HTTPS URL answers 301 with `Location: https://shop.example.com/`, which then redirects to itself. `sudo nginx -T | grep -n try_files`.
`try_files / =404;` checks for a directory named `/` and redirects. Use `try_files $uri $uri/ =404;` in `/etc/nginx/sites-available/shop`, then `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`.

questions.prompt: Which request header decides which nginx server block answers?
Which status code did every HTTPS page return before your fix?

checks.describe: HTTPS pages answer 200/404 without redirects; HTTP redirects once to HTTPS

tasks.title: Trust the internal CA
tasks.text:
Run the health check without `-k` and read the error. `curl -v` shows the certificate's issuer. `-k` turns off verification, so it would also accept an attacker's certificate. It's never the fix.

The server certificate is fine: it's signed by our internal CA, which this machine doesn't know yet. Add the CA to the **system** trust store, so curl and every other program on the box verify it. Done when `curl https://shop.example.com/health` prints `ok` without `-k`.
hints: Ubuntu reads extra CAs from `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/*.crt`: `sudo cp /etc/ssl/example-ca/ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/example-internal-ca.crt && sudo update-ca-certificates`.

questions.prompt: Which curl option skips certificate verification (and must not be the fix)?
Which command rebuilds Ubuntu's CA bundle after you add a .crt file?

checks.describe: the system trust store contains the internal CA; curl verifies the site without -k

walkthrough:
### What was broken
1. The provisioning script wrote `try_files / =404;` in the HTTPS server block. For every URL nginx found the "directory" `/` and sent a **301** to `https://shop.example.com/`, which redirected to itself: a loop.
2. The certificate is signed by "Example Internal CA", which was not in the system trust store, so verification failed with `unable to get local issuer certificate`.
3. "Welcome to nginx" was not a bug: `curl http://127.0.0.1/` sends `Host: 127.0.0.1`, which matches no `server_name`, so the **default server** answered.

### Task 1
```bash
curl -sI http://127.0.0.1/ | head -1                     # 200, default site
curl -sI http://shop.example.com/ | grep -i location     # https://shop.example.com/
curl -skIL --max-redirs 5 https://shop.example.com/docs/ # 301 -> https://shop.example.com/ -> 301 -> ... Maximum (5) redirects followed
sudo nginx -T | grep -n 'try_files'
sudo sed -i 's|try_files / =404;|try_files $uri $uri/ =404;|' /etc/nginx/sites-available/shop
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{num_redirects}\n' -L https://shop.example.com/docs/   # 200 0
```
*Why:* `-I` shows only headers, `-L` follows `Location`, `-w` prints facts such as `%{http_code}` and `%{redirect_url}`. A redirect whose target is the same URL is always a loop. A browser hides this; curl shows every hop.

### Task 2
```bash
curl -sS https://shop.example.com/health                # curl: (60) ... unable to get local issuer certificate
curl -v https://shop.example.com/health 2>&1 | grep -i issuer   # issuer: O=Example Org; CN=Example Internal CA
sudo cp /etc/ssl/example-ca/ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/example-internal-ca.crt
sudo update-ca-certificates                             # 1 added
curl -sS https://shop.example.com/health                # ok
```
*Why:* the file must end in `.crt` in that directory. `update-ca-certificates` rebuilds `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, which curl, wget, Python, apt and most other tools use. Some runtimes keep their own store (Java keystore, Node's `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`), so check them too.

**Source (adapted):** [ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS after adding SSL using LE](https://community.letsencrypt.org/t/err-too-many-redirects-after-adding-ssl-using-le/81291): the port-80 redirect was fine. The loop came from `try_files / =404;` in the 443 block, which made https redirect to https. Changing it to `try_files $uri $uri/ =404;` fixed it.
